evidence.quote: by and between Harbor Point Construction, Inc., a California corporation
evidence.rationale: The preamble names Harbor Point Construction, Inc. as "Contractor".

evidence.quote: and Delta Mechanical Systems, LLC, a California limited liability company
evidence.rationale: The preamble names Delta Mechanical Systems, LLC as "Subcontractor".

evidence.quote: Sacramento Unified School District ("Owner")
evidence.rationale: The Recitals define Owner.

project.value: Rosemont Elementary Modernization, 9594 Mormon Street, Sacramento, California 95827

evidence.quote: for construction of the project known as Rosemont Elementary Modernization, located at 9594 Mormon Street, Sacramento, California 95827
evidence.rationale: The Recitals define the Project.

evidence.quote: This Subcontract is governed by the laws of the State of California, without regard to its conflict-of-laws
evidence.rationale: Section 17.1 is the governing-law clause.

evidence.quote: The parties have agreed in writing, by this Subcontract, that Contractor's payment to Subcontractor is due on a pay-when-paid basis
evidence.rationale: Section 6.3 expressly states pay-when-paid and says the provision governs timing only. Section 6.2 ties payment to 7 days after Owner payment.

evidence.quote: within seven (7) days after Contractor receives payment from Owner for that Subcontract Work
evidence.rationale: Section 6.2 states the 7-day period.

evidence.quote: The parties have agreed in writing, by this Subcontract, that Contractor's payment to Subcontractor is due on a pay-when-paid basis
evidence.rationale: A specific period is written in Section 6.2, and Section 6.3 states written agreement.

evidence.quote: Contractor shall withhold retention of ten percent (10%) from each progress payment otherwise due to Subcontractor under this Subcontract.
evidence.rationale: Section 7.1 sets the rate at 10%. The 5% figure in the Recitals is Owner's retention against Contractor, not the subcontract rate.

release_condition.value: (a) Final Completion of the Subcontract Work, and (b) Contractor's receipt of retention from Owner for the Subcontract Work

evidence.quote: both of the following have occurred: (a) Final Completion of the Subcontract Work, and (b) Contractor's receipt of retention from Owner for the Subcontract Work.
evidence.rationale: Section 7.3 states both conditions. Section 7.4 adds pre-release document deliveries.

evidence.quote: Contractor shall release retention to Subcontractor within ten (10) days after both of the following have occurred
evidence.rationale: Section 7.3 states the 10-day period.

evidence.quote: As a condition of each progress payment, Subcontractor shall deliver to Contractor a conditional waiver and release on progress payment covering the amount requested
evidence.rationale: Section 5.1 requires a conditional progress waiver.

evidence.quote: Within five (5) days after receipt of each progress payment, Subcontractor shall deliver to Contractor an unconditional waiver and release on progress payment
evidence.rationale: Section 5.2 requires an unconditional waiver after each payment.

evidence.quote: Subcontractor shall obtain and deliver to Contractor conditional and unconditional waivers and releases from each of its lower-tier subcontractors and material suppliers
evidence.rationale: Section 5.4 requires lower-tier waivers.

evidence.quote: All waivers and releases furnished under this Subcontract must be in the statutory form prescribed by California Civil Code Sections 8132 through 8138
evidence.rationale: Section 5.3 requires the statutory forms.

evidence.quote: Contractor may set off against any payment due to Subcontractor under this Subcontract the amount of any backcharge for costs incurred by Contractor because of Subcontractor's failure to perform
evidence.rationale: Section 9.1 grants a backcharge setoff, subject to written notice and 48 hours to cure where practicable.

evidence.quote: Contractor may withhold from any payment an amount sufficient to correct defective or nonconforming Subcontract Work
evidence.rationale: Section 9.2 allows withholding for defective work. Section 9.3 adds withholding for claims and missing payrolls or waivers.

evidence.quote: Contractor will make no payment for materials or equipment stored on site or off site that have not been incorporated into the Project
evidence.rationale: Section 6.4 expressly excludes payment for stored materials.

anomalies.description: Subcontract retention (10%) is double the retention Owner withholds from Contractor under the Prime Contract (5%). Do not use the 5% Recital figure as the subcontract rate. A controller should note the mismatch.

evidence.quote: Under the Prime Contract, Owner withholds five percent (5%) retention from Contractor on each progress payment.
evidence.rationale: Subcontract retention (10%) is double the retention Owner withholds from Contractor under the Prime Contract (5%). Do not use the 5% Recital figure as the subcontract rate. A controller should note the mismatch.

anomalies.description: Retention release depends on Contractor's receipt of retention from Owner, with no outside date if Owner does not release.

evidence.quote: (b) Contractor's receipt of retention from Owner for the Subcontract Work.
evidence.rationale: Retention release depends on Contractor's receipt of retention from Owner, with no outside date if Owner does not release.

anomalies.description: Additional preconditions to retention release include a final conditional waiver, lower-tier final waivers, warranties and payroll evidence.

evidence.quote: Before release of retention, Subcontractor shall furnish a conditional waiver and release on final payment as described in Article 5, together with final lower-tier waivers
evidence.rationale: Additional preconditions to retention release include a final conditional waiver, lower-tier final waivers, warranties and payroll evidence.

anomalies.description: Contractor may apply retention to any amount owed by Subcontractor, including Article 9 amounts. This is a broad setoff right against retention.

evidence.quote: Contractor may apply retention to any amount owed by Subcontractor to Contractor under this Subcontract, including amounts described in Article 9.
evidence.rationale: Contractor may apply retention to any amount owed by Subcontractor, including Article 9 amounts. This is a broad setoff right against retention.

anomalies.description: Release of amounts withheld for defective work depends on correction to the satisfaction of Contractor, the Architect and the Inspector of Record, which is a discretionary standard.

evidence.quote: until that Subcontract Work has been corrected to the satisfaction of Contractor, the Architect, and the Inspector of Record.
evidence.rationale: Release of amounts withheld for defective work depends on correction to the satisfaction of Contractor, the Architect and the Inspector of Record, which is a discretionary standard.

anomalies.description: For Owner-initiated changes, Subcontractor's price adjustment is capped at what Contractor actually receives from Owner. This is a pay-if-paid-type risk shift limited to change orders.

evidence.quote: Subcontractor's adjustment in price and time will not exceed the amount Contractor actually receives from Owner for that portion of the change attributable to the Subcontract Work.
evidence.rationale: For Owner-initiated changes, Subcontractor's price adjustment is capped at what Contractor actually receives from Owner. This is a pay-if-paid-type risk shift limited to change orders.

anomalies.description: On termination for convenience, payment is limited to amounts Contractor recovers from Owner.

evidence.quote: plus reasonable demobilization costs, to the extent Contractor recovers those amounts from Owner.
evidence.rationale: On termination for convenience, payment is limited to amounts Contractor recovers from Owner.

anomalies.description: The contract does not address payment by joint check.
